A laser distance meter is a hand-held device which uses a laser, usually a green or red laser diode, to measure the distance between the device and a point. Laser distance meters provide a very quick measure of relatively short to moderately long distances. A laser distance meter also can function as an ultrasonic device and can be used to measure distance and thickness, as well as height. For long distances they are often mounted on a tripod and connected via a cable to a laptop. The typical measurement precision is 0.2 mm. Laser distance meters, in common use, display distances in feet and meters (or centimeters), with a few exceptions that offer other unit-system displays. The most common color laser is a 532 nm diode, which has a wavelength of green light but is perceived by the human eye as red light. If the laser is designed for measuring wall thickness, it may emit infrared light, typically at 780 nm, which has an invisible wavelength and can be shielded by clothing.
Fluke and other laser distance meters also use laser beams to detect obstacles at the far end of the laser beam, using infrared signals to detect "hot spots" such as humans, plants, or metal objects within the beam

Originally used for missile guidance systems, when this system was declassified it helped many people, such as painters learning about proportions. The pulsed nature of the source made it possible to have a more controlled and precise measurement, due to the fact that you can have a stable target and the laser pulse will be received in a short time.
